claim: On 2026-08-05 Lambda added scalable network bandwidth for functions outside a VPC with 2 GB of memory or more: bandwidth scales from 625 Mbps at 2 GB up to 3,000 Mbps at 10 GB, where before the limit was 625 Mbps; you enable it with a request through AWS Service Quotas under the Network bandwidth per execution environment quota.

qualifiers.scope: per execution environment, functions outside a VPC
qualifiers.condition: after a Service Quotas request; functions with 2 GB of memory or more

evidence.quote: This feature enables functions outside a VPC configured with 2 GB of memory or more to access network bandwidth that scales proportionally, from 625 Mbps at 2 GB up to 3,000 Mbps at 10 GB.
As data volume and performance requirements grow, the existing limit of 625 Mbps can constrain data transfer speeds to and from an execution environment.

evidence.heading: AWS Lambda announces scalable network bandwidth up to 3,000 Mbps for functions outside a VPC

evidence.quote: To get started, submit a request through AWS Service Quotas under the Network bandwidth per execution environment quota to enable scalable network bandwidth on your account.
